_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) who have received prior treatment with 3 or more kinase inhibitors, including imatinib.

pivotal_trials.design: International, multi-center, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic GIST who had been previously treated with imatinib, sunitinib, and regorafenib
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival (PFS) based on blinded independent central review using RECIST v1.1 modified for GIST
pivotal_trials.result: Median PFS 6.3 months (95% CI 4.6, 6.9) for ripretinib vs 1.0 months (95% CI 0.9, 1.7) for placebo; HR 0.15 (95% CI 0.09, 0.25); p<0.0001. ORR 9% (95% CI 4.2, 18) vs 0% (not statistically significant). Median OS 15.1 months vs 6.6 months; HR 0.36 (95% CI 0.21, 0.62), not formally tested.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=20%): alopecia (52%), fatigue (42%), nausea (39%), abdominal pain (36%), constipation (34%), myalgia, diarrhea, decreased appetite, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia (PPES, 21%), and vomiting. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 31% of patients. Most common Grade 3/4 laboratory abnormalities (>=4%): increased lipase and decreased phosphate.
target_moa: Ripretinib is a small molecule, switch-control tyrosine kinase inhibitor that inhibits KIT and PDGFR-alpha mutated kinases.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the review team did not refer the application to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee.

orphan_indication.text: Ripretinib was granted orphan drug designation for treatment of GIST.

citations.quote: Ripretinib was granted orphan drug designation for treatment of GIST and in accordance with 21 CFR 314.55(5)(d), orphan drugs are exempt from the pediatric study requirements in 21 CFR 314.55.

basis.text: The application was designated Priority review.

summary.text: Ripretinib (QINLOCK) received regular (full) approval under 21 CFR 314.50 based on the single pivotal Phase 3 INVICTUS trial. The application had orphan drug designation for GIST and was granted Priority review, with a PDUFA goal date of August 13, 2020.

citations.quote: The recommendation for regular approval of ripretinib, according to 21 CFR, Part 314.50, Subpart B, is based primarily on efficacy and safety results of a single trial, Study DCC-2618-03-001 (also referred to as INVICTUS).
